ucs.title: [LLM] APT32 (OceanLotus / Canvas Cyclone / BISMUTH) DLL side-loading via hijacked AV / vendor binaries in user-writable paths
ucs.description: Hunts APT32's signature execution chain: dropping a legitimately-signed, vendor-trusted binary (Symantec RasTls, Avast wsc_proxy, McAfee mcoemcpy, Adobe AcroTranscoder, Intel igfxEM, ASUS WSPanel, Sophos SemBackup) into a user-writable directory so it side-loads a co-located malicious DLL (KerrDown / Denis / Roland / PhantomNet loader). Stock locations for these binaries are %ProgramFiles%; observing them executing from %AppData%, %Temp%, %ProgramData%, %Public% or %Downloads% is the OceanLotus hallmark documented by Cybereason (Cobalt Kitty), ESET, and Mandiant.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("wsc_proxy.exe","wsc_proxy_64.exe","rastls.exe","rastlsc.exe","RasTls.exe","AcroTranscoder.exe","SemBackup.exe","AsusWSPanel.exe","mcoemcpy.exe","mctray.exe","igfxEM.exe","GoogleUpdate.exe","smcgui.exe") AND (Processes.process_path="*\\AppData\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\ProgramData\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Public\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Downloads\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\PerfLogs\\*") AND NOT (Processes.process_path="*\\Program Files*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Windows\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | where NOT match(user,"(?i).*\$$")
ucs.kql:
let AbusedSignedBins = dynamic(["wsc_proxy.exe","wsc_proxy_64.exe","rastls.exe","rastlsc.exe","acrotranscoder.exe","sembackup.exe","asuswspanel.exe","mcoemcpy.exe","mctray.exe","igfxem.exe","smcgui.exe","googleupdate.exe"]);
let UserWritable = dynamic([@"\appdata\", @"\temp\", @"\programdata\", @"\users\public\", @"\downloads\", @"\perflogs\"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ (AbusedSignedBins)
| where FolderPath has_any (UserWritable)
| where FolderPath !has @"\program files" and FolderPath !has @"\windows\"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName endswith ".dll"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, LoadedDll = FileName, LoadedDllFolder = FolderPath, LoadingProc = InitiatingProcessFileName, LoadingProcPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath
  ) on DeviceId
| where LoadingProc =~ FileName and LoadedDllFolder =~ FolderPath
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          LoadedDll, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let AbusedSignedBins = dynamic(["wsc_proxy.exe","wsc_proxy_64.exe","rastls.exe","rastlsc.exe","acrotranscoder.exe","sembackup.exe","asuswspanel.exe","mcoemcpy.exe","mctray.exe","igfxem.exe","smcgui.exe","googleupdate.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend BinName = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, @"\\")[-1]))
| where BinName in (AbusedSignedBins)
| where NewProcessName has_any (@"\AppData\", @"\Temp\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Public\", @"\Downloads\", @"\PerfLogs\")
| where NewProcessName !has @"\Program Files" and NewProcessName !has @"\Windows\\"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$" and TargetUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: APT32 OceanLotus DLL Side-Loading via Hijacked Vendor Binary
id: 8c9c0f4a-1f6e-4d20-93b4-a7c2e1f9d310
status: experimental
description: Detects APT32 (OceanLotus / Canvas Cyclone / BISMUTH) staging a legitimately-signed AV or vendor binary in a user-writable path so it side-loads a co-located malicious DLL (KerrDown / Denis / Roland loaders).
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
  - https://www.cybereason.com/blog/operation-cobalt-kitty-a-large-scale-apt-in-asia-carried-out-by-the-oceanlotus-group
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\wsc_proxy.exe'
      - '\wsc_proxy_64.exe'
      - '\rastls.exe'
      - '\rastlsc.exe'
      - '\RasTls.exe'
      - '\AcroTranscoder.exe'
      - '\SemBackup.exe'
      - '\AsusWSPanel.exe'
      - '\mcoemcpy.exe'
      - '\mctray.exe'
      - '\igfxEM.exe'
      - '\smcgui.exe'
      - '\GoogleUpdate.exe'
  selection_path:
    Image|contains:
      - '\AppData\'
      - '\Temp\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
      - '\Public\'
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\PerfLogs\'
  filter_legit:
    Image|contains:
      - '\Program Files'
      - '\Windows\'
  condition: selection_image and selection_path and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Vendor self-extracting installers running from %Temp% on first launch (validate signing chain + file path)
level: high
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1574.002
  - attack.g0050
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\wsc_proxy.exe OR *\\WSC_PROXY.exe OR *\\wsc_proxy_64.exe OR *\\rastls.exe OR *\\RasTls.exe OR *\\rastlsc.exe OR *\\AcroTranscoder.exe OR *\\acrotranscoder.exe OR *\\SemBackup.exe OR *\\sembackup.exe OR *\\AsusWSPanel.exe OR *\\mcoemcpy.exe OR *\\mctray.exe OR *\\igfxEM.exe OR *\\igfxem.exe OR *\\smcgui.exe OR *\\GoogleUpdate.exe OR *\\googleupdate.exe) @Image:(*\\AppData\\* OR *\\appdata\\* OR *\\Temp\\* OR *\\temp\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\* OR *\\programdata\\* OR *\\Public\\* OR *\\public\\* OR *\\Downloads\\* OR *\\downloads\\* OR *\\PerfLogs\\* OR *\\perflogs\\*) -@Image:(*\\Program\ Files* OR *\\Windows\\*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(wsc_proxy|wsc_proxy_64|rastls|rastlsc|acrotranscoder|sembackup|asuswspanel|mcoemcpy|mctray|igfxem|smcgui|googleupdate)\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(appdata|temp|programdata|public|downloads|perflogs)\\/i
| NOT ImageFileName=/\\(program files|windows)\\/i
| UserName!=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
| count > 0
ucs.rationale: DLL side-loading from misplaced signed vendor binaries is the most consistent OceanLotus / Cobalt Kitty fingerprint across a decade of campaigns — Cybereason documented Symantec, Kaspersky and McAfee binaries side-loaded from %AppData% in the original Cobalt Kitty intrusion, ESET tied the same chain to Roland and PhantomNet, and Microsoft (BISMUTH / Canvas Cyclone) saw it again with Adobe AcroTran

ucs.title: [LLM] APT32 OceanLotus Outlook Home Page / Office Test DLL persistence registry write
ucs.description: Hunts APT32's distinctive Office Application Startup persistence: writing the `Office test\Special\Perf` registry value (loads an arbitrary DLL into every Office process) or hijacking the Outlook WebView / Home Page URL to load remote HTML+script on Outlook launch. Both were detailed in the Cobalt Kitty (Cybereason) and BISMUTH (Microsoft) write-ups as how OceanLotus survives reboot on diaspora-targeted journalist / ASEAN workstations.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_path="*\\Software\\Microsoft\\Office test\\Special\\Perf*" OR (Registry.registry_path="*\\Outlook\\WebView\\*" AND Registry.registry_value_name="URL") OR Registry.registry_path="*\\Outlook\\Today\\*" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\Outlook\\Home Page*") AND Registry.action IN ("modified","created","set") by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data Registry.process_name Registry.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | where NOT match(user,"(?i).*\$$") AND (like(registry_value_data,"%http%") OR like(registry_value_data,"%.dll%") OR like(registry_path,"%Office test%"))
ucs.kql:
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where (RegistryKey has @"\Software\Microsoft\Office test\Special\Perf"
      or (RegistryKey has @"\Outlook\WebView\" and RegistryValueName =~ "URL")
      or (RegistryKey has @"\Outlook\Today\" and RegistryValueName =~ "URL")
      or RegistryKey has @"\Outlook\Home Page")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has @"\Office test\Special\Perf"
     or RegistryValueData matches regex @"(?i)https?://"
     or RegistryValueData has ".dll"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ActionType,
          RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventType in~ ("RegistryValueSet","Set","RegistryKeyCreated","Create")
| where (RegistryKey has @"\Software\Microsoft\Office test\Special\Perf"
      or (RegistryKey has @"\Outlook\WebView\" and RegistryValue =~ "URL")
      or (RegistryKey has @"\Outlook\Today\" and RegistryValue =~ "URL")
      or RegistryKey has @"\Outlook\Home Page")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has @"\Office test\Special\Perf"
     or RegistryValueData matches regex @"(?i)https?://"
     or RegistryValueData has ".dll"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType,
          RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 (@TargetObject:(*\\Office\ test\\Special\\Perf* OR *\\office\ test\\Special\\Perf*) OR (@TargetObject:(*\\Outlook\\WebView\\* OR *\\outlook\\webview\\* OR *\\Outlook\\Today\\* OR *\\outlook\\today\\*) AND @Details:(*http* OR *HTTP*)) OR @TargetObject:(*\\Outlook\\Home\ Page* OR *\\outlook\\home\ page*))
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| RegObjectName=/(Office test\\Special\\Perf|Outlook\\WebView|Outlook\\Today|Outlook\\Home Page)/i
| (RegObjectName=/Office test\\Special\\Perf/i OR RegStringValue=/https?:\/\//i OR RegStringValue=/\.dll/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RegObjectName, RegValueName, RegStringValue, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
| count > 0
ucs.rationale: The `Office test\Special\Perf` key (T1137.002) has virtually zero legitimate use — its presence on any user-context endpoint is itself the IoC. Pairing it with Outlook WebView / Home Page URL hijacks (the OceanLotus PowerShell-staged variant Cybereason recovered from the Cobalt Kitty operation, where Outlook re-opened the attacker's HTML each launch) covers both flavours of APT32 Office persistenc
